pass: The Maryland member-page cohort -- every voter-visible, still-seated stance key whose ONLY source is an mgaleg Members/Details roster page.

cohort_measured_fresh.note: The recorded backlog called this '932 MD member-page keys'. That number came from an 08-11 source-class precedence I could not reproduce, so it was re-measured against production rather than inherited: 521 voter-visible, still-seated, member-page-ONLY keys across 88 legislators. 1,665 keys cite a member page among other sources; 521 cite ONLY one. Both numbers are stated so the next reader need not guess which is meant.

headline: 70% OF THIS COHORT IS SOUND. 367 of 521 rows carry a sponsorship that is verifiable against the member's own mgaleg record. The detector flagged the whole class because the URL is a roster page -- but a roster page LISTS THE MEMBER'S BILLS, so for most of these rows it is genuinely the evidence. The right disposition for the bulk of the MD backlog is a CITATION REPAIR, not retirement. Treating it as a retirement queue would have destroyed hundreds of true rows.
method: Every bill each of the 88 legislators sponsored or co-sponsored in 2023RS, 2024RS, 2025RS and 2026RS was read from mgaleg's own per-session member record (Members/Details/<slug>?ys=<session>). That is mgaleg's OWN attribution, so the surname twin (md_sponsor_identity_traps 2) cannot bite, and the Primary/Co-Sponsor label excludes the crossfile companions that trap 8 warns about. A member page defaults to the CURRENT session only, so each session was fetched explicitly. Trap 5 is honoured: a session with no record (no session portrait) is marked UNAVAILABLE, never read as an absence.
four_passes_each_rescuing_rows: Pass 1 matched Title-Case spans only -> 162 NO_INSTRUMENT.

Pass 2 added contiguous content-token runs for paraphrased titles and moved 113 rows out, 64 of them straight off the blank list. April Miller and April Rose describe HB0460 as "solar energy construction restrictions in priority preservation areas" -- it is genuinely theirs, and pass 1 would have blanked a TRUE claim.
Pass 3 added reordered paraphrases (bag-of-words coverage) and explicit bill NUMBERS.
Pass 4 was hand-reading all 72 survivors, which is how the composed-citation class surfaced.
THE FIRST CUT OVER-FIRES. It did here four times running, and each correction rescued rows a blank would have destroyed.

class_1_no_instrument.finding: A roster page states who someone IS and lists the bills they put their name to. IT CARRIES NO POSITION. These rows name no bill, no vote and no statement, and reach a chair from party, district or role alone -- "Backed progressive revenue measures and tax equity legislation", "As a Baltimore City Democrat ... supports comprehensive clean energy legislation". A PARTY IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT (the rule that blanked Morales and Campos in 1897).
class_1_no_instrument.concentration: taxes 25, public-safety-approach 24, civil-rights 11 -- the topics where a party label feels most like an answer.

class_2_composed_citations.the_subtler_half: THREE cite a bill the member REALLY DID SPONSOR and invent its subject. Veronica Turner's HB0478 (2026) is hers -- it is "Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Classroom Supplies Purchased by Teachers", not "Immigration Enforcement Agreements - Prohibition" (that is HB0444). Her HB0347 is hers -- "Workers' Compensation - Occupational Disease Presumptions - Hypertension", not a "Voting Rights Act of 2026". Valderrama's HB0997 is hers -- "State Finance and Procurement - Prevailing Wage Rate", not "Real Property - Short-Term Rentals". THE NUMBER CHECKS OUT AND ONLY THE SUBJECT IS INVENTED, so the citation looks maximally verifiable and is false only on inspection.
class_2_composed_citations.one_row_in_this_set_is_NOT_a_defect: Mary A. Lehman / housing cites HB 693 (2024) = the Renters' Rights and Stabilization Act of 2024, real housing legislation, AND SHE IS AMONG ITS SPONSORS. Left alone. Ben Barnes cites the same bill, is NOT a sponsor, and his row claims only that he "supported" it -- his is blanked. Same citation, two verdicts, decided by reading the sponsor list.

the_bug_that_nearly_produced_a_mass_fals: The first bill-number run took the session only from a parenthesised year like "(2023)". Claims are written "(SB0977 2025)" just as often, so the year was missed and the fallback tried 2023RS FIRST. MARYLAND RENUMBERS EVERY SESSION, so that compared a 2025 bill against the unrelated 2023 bill sharing its number and reported a mismatch EVERY time -- it briefly looked as though almost every cited bill number in Maryland was fabricated. Fixed by taking the year NEAREST the number mention and recording which session was used in every verdict. WHEN A CHECK FAILS FOR EVERYTHING, SUSPECT THE CHECK.

correction_to_migration_1897.what_was_wrong: 1897 said Steve Johnson's member page "lists 150 bills for the 2025 and 2026 sessions". A member page shows the CURRENT session only, so that reading covered 2026RS alone. Its control count "Solar 0" was an artefact of that one-session window.
correction_to_migration_1897.what_is_true: All four sessions of his term were read (117, 118, 123, 90 sponsorships). He co-sponsored HB0300 (2023RS) "School Buildings - Solar Technology - Solar Panels on Schools" and HB1233 (2025RS) "Community Solar Energy Generating Systems - Subscription Eligibility" -- both EXPANDING solar, the opposite of the restrictive siting bill his row attributed to him.
correction_to_migration_1897.the_blanks_stand: The claimed bill is still not his: HB0460 (2026RS) "Solar Energy - Construction of Generating Stations in Priority Preservation Areas and Study" is co-sponsored by Delegates April Miller and April Rose, both REPUBLICANS, and Johnson is not among them -- which independently confirms 1897's finding that his rows carried a Republican's record. "Fair Districts" 0, "Scholarship" 0, "Voter" 0 and "Citizenship" 0 across all four sessions. He is a CO-SPONSOR of two police accountability bills (HB0885 2025RS, HB0508 2026RS), contradicting the row that said he opposed such reforms.
correction_to_migration_1897.action: All eight blanks keep value 0; their reasoning is rewritten in place because it is shown to voters.

blocked.reason: `immigration` has NO Season 2 pin, so no blank can be written.
blocked.running_total: With the 3 blocked by migration 1896 and the 3 by 1897, 26 defective chairs now stand unfixable on that one topic. It is the largest blocked defect in the audit and belongs to the Season 3 decision.

recorded_not_fixed.VOTE_CLAIM: 35 rows claim a VOTE. A SPONSORSHIP INDEX CANNOT TEST A VOTE -- these need MD roll calls and are untouched. Calling them absent would have been a false negative; the first cut did exactly that before the class was split out.
recorded_not_fixed.PARTIAL_and_out_of_window: 30 rows have weak title overlap, or belong to members seated before 2023 whose claim may reference an earlier session. Absence is only provable inside the sessions actually read, so none of these is called absent. They need a human and, for the long-serving members, sessions earlier than the four read here.
recorded_not_fixed.MATCHED_and_PARAPHRASE_MATCH: 367 rows have a verified sponsorship and are LEFT ALONE. Whether the sponsorship seats the chair at the right rung is a separate ladder question, not a sourcing one. The useful follow-up for these is a citation repair pointing at the bill page, which would clear them from the generic-source queue without touching a single chair.
